title: Shakespeare takes the stage in Laredo: TAMIU's free Shakespeare Fest returns Nov. 6–12
excerpt: Texas A&M International University's weeklong Shakespeare Fest runs Nov. 6–12 at TAMIU's Center for the Fine and Performing Arts and the Laredo Center for the Arts. All events are free and open to the public, from Texas Shakespeare Roadshow performances to a first-of-its-kind Día de los Muertos lecture.
content:
If music be the food of love, play on — and head to Laredo this November. Texas A&M International University (TAMIU) will celebrate the city's longstanding connection to the works of William Shakespeare during Shakespeare Fest 2026, a weeklong festival of theatrical performances, literary exploration and the fine arts, according to TAMIU (Oct. 15, 2026).

The celebration runs Friday, Nov. 6, through Thursday, Nov. 12, at TAMIU's Center for the Fine and Performing Arts and the Laredo Center for the Arts — and every event is free and open to the public.

Headlining the week are theatrical performances by the traveling cast of the Kilgore College-based Texas Shakespeare Festival's Roadshow. The troupe performs "Shakespeare's Greatest Hits" at 2 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 6, and "Twelfth Night" at 7:30 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 7, both at the Center for the Fine and Performing Arts Theatre. It is the fourth year the Roadshow has brought Shakespeare to TAMIU, and the festival has been praised by the Texas Commission on the Arts as one of the state's top cultural events.

This year's standout addition is a first-of-its-kind lecture, "Día de los Muertos & Borderlands Shakespeare," by Dr. Adrianna Santos, associate professor at Texas A&M University-San Antonio, set for 5:30 p.m. on Nov. 6 at the Laredo Center for the Arts. The lecture explores how Día de los Muertos traditions and Indigenous Mexican and Latinx perspectives reshape Shakespeare's themes of life, death and the afterlife — bringing the festival into historic downtown Laredo.

Rounding out the week: a "History of Shakespeare in Laredo" exhibit on display 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. in the Center for the Fine and Performing Arts lobby, and a silent Shakespeare film adaptation accompanied by a performance from Dr. Colin Campbell, university organist and associate professor of music, at 7:30 p.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, in the recital hall.

Organized by the University's College of Arts and Sciences Department of Humanities, the festival pays tribute to the Bard through film, theater and a borderland-themed lecture, explained Dr. Kaitlyn Chacon, associate professor of English. She called the festival an opportunity to bring Shakespeare's works to life while celebrating the arts, the humanities and the power of storytelling — and to show how his work keeps resonating with audiences today.

Although all events are free, organizers encourage attendees to register at go.tamiu.edu/shakespeare. For more information, contact Chacon at kaitlyn.culliton@tamiu.edu.

Sources: Texas A&M International University (tamiu.edu), "TAMIU Shakespeare Fest Set for Nov. 6-12" (Oct. 15, 2026).
